document.title: About Me
document.description: Meet Erkan — a QA engineer bridging Web2 and Web3 testing worlds with practical insights, real-world examples, and a focus on making blockchain technology more secure and reliable.

body.raw:
### 👋 About Me

Hey, I'm **Erkan** — a QA engineer who's been working in tech and **blockchain** for quite a while now.  
Over the years, I've tested everything from traditional web systems to decentralized apps, wallets, and smart contracts.

I created **web3qa.com** to share what I've learned about **testing blockchain technologies in the real world** — focusing on reproducible results, practical examples, and clarity over hype.  
My goal is simple: help testers, auditors, and developers make Web3 **more secure, reliable, and transparent** — one verified test case at a time.

---

### 🔗 Connect
You can find me on [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/erkan-barin/) — always happy to connect with other QA engineers and blockchain enthusiasts.

document.title: Fuzzing
document.description: Fuzzing is an automated testing technique that generates many pseudo-random inputs to explore unexpected execution paths and uncover edge case bugs.

body.raw:
# Fuzzing

Fuzzing supplies a broad distribution of inputs to a target function or contract to surface crashes, assertion failures, and invariant violations that handcrafted tests might miss.

## Benefits

- Discovers edge cases
- Increases confidence in validation logic
- Complements unit and integration tests

## Related Terms

Property-based testing, invariant checking.

document.description: This guide introduces foundational approaches to testing EVM smart contracts covering unit tests, property fuzzing, and security invariant patterns.

body.raw:
import React from 'react';

# Intro to Testing Smart Contracts

Testing smart contracts mitigates risk, documents intent, and enables safe iteration.

## Approaches

1. Unit tests: assert deterministic logic.
2. Property-based / fuzz tests: explore unexpected inputs.
3. Invariant monitoring: ensure system constraints always hold.

{/* Example code placeholder */}

## Next Steps

Continue with deeper guides on gas profiling and formal verification.
